Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gQv.ph DILG OPINION No. 37 s. 2022 May 16, 2022 ATTY. JORICO FAVOR BAYAUA Vice Mayor Municipality of Conner Province of Apayao Dear Vice Mayor Bayaua: This has reference to your letter dated 09 February 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on whether or not an incumbent elected official may continue giving ayuda or financial assistance during the campaign period using the funds of his or her office, if his or her relative, whether by consanguinity or affinity is running for public office, and whether such action is considered vote-buying, or among those prohibited acts during the campaign period. Per your letter, the Office of the Municipal Social Welfare and Development (MSWD), which is under the Office of the Mayor of Conner, Apayao has launched a program of providing financial assistance to the constituents of Conner. While the incumbent Mayor, Hon. Martina W. Dangoy, is not a candidate for any elective position in the upcoming 2022 elections, her husband, Mr. Leonardo Dangoy, is running for Mayor of Conner. Hence, your query. In this regard, Sec. 261 (a) of the Omnibus Election Code provides: "Sec. 261. Prohibited Acts. - The following shall be guilty of an election offense: a. Vote-buying and vote-selling. 1. Any person who gives, offers or promises money or anything of value, gives or promises any office or employment, franchise or grant, public or private, or makes or offers to make an expenditure, directly or indirectly, or cause an expenditure to be made to any person, association, corporation, entity, or community in order to induce anyone or the public in general to vote for or against any candidate or withhold his vote in the election, or to vote for or against any aspirant for the nomination or choice of a candidate in a convention or similar selection process of a political party. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

2. Any person, association, corporation, group or community who solicits or receives, directly or indirectly, any expenditure or promise of any office or employment, public or private, for any of the foregoing considerations. " Further, the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) issued Resolution Number 10747 dated December 16, 2021 , prohibiting the release of any public funds starting March 25, 2022 until May 08, 2022 except for limited purposes. Section 2 of the said Resolution provides: "Section 2. Prohibition on Release, Disbursement or Expenditure of Public Funds. — Effective March 25, 2022 until May 08, 2022, no public official or employee, including barangay officials, and those of govemment-owned or controlled corporations and their subsidiaries, shall release, disburse, or expend any public funds for: x xxx 3. The Department for Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and any other office. aqency. or bureau in other departments of the government performinq functions similar to said department, except for salaries of personnel, and for such other expenses as the Commission may authorize after due notice and hearing. x x x x" (emphasis supplied) We submit that providing financial assistance to the constituents per se does not constitute vote-buying, except when it is done within the period specified in COMELEC Resolution No. 10747, which should start from March 25, 2022 until May 8, 2022. Giving of financial assistance within the period specified will be considered vote- buying, and therefore, constitutes election offense, penalized under Section 21 of Resolution No. 10747, viz: "Section 21. Penalty — Any violation of the provisions of this Resolution shall, consistent with Sections 261 and 264 of the Omnibus Election Code, constitute an election offense and shall be punishable by imprisonment of not less than one (I) year but not more than six (6) years, among other penalties for by law." The foregoing prohibition is without regard on whether an incumbent local elective official's relative is running for public office or not in the same local govemment unit. Page 2 of 3

Be that as it may, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion that will be rendered by a more competent authority or the court. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN MAR Undersec ary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS/LRALLD/1asm Copy fumished: DIR.
